:::{#sol-epe-split-bias}

Insert the expected prediction:

$$
\ba
\truemeanf{\predvar} - \predval
&= \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \Epredval} + \paren{\Epredval - \predval}
&& \text{(add and subtract } \Epredval \text{)}
\ea
$$

Square it:

$$
\ba
\sqf{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \predval}
&= \sqf{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \Epredval}
+ 2 \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \Epredval} \paren{\Epredval - \predval}
+ \sqf{\Epredval - \predval}
&& \text{(expand the square of a sum)}
\ea
$$

Take the expectation of each term in turn.

The first term does not depend on $\trainset$:
$\truemeanf{\predvar}$ is a constant,
and $\Epredval$ has already been averaged over training sets.
The expectation of a constant is that constant:

$$
\ba
\E{\sqf{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \Epredval}}
&= \sqf{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \Epredval}
&& \text{(expectation of a constant)} \\
&= \sqf{\Epredval - \truemeanf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(a number and its negative have the same square)} \\
&= \sqf{\bias{\predval}}
&& \text{(} \bias{\predval} = \Epredval - \truemeanf{\predvar} \text{, @thm-prediction-bias-average-fit)}
\ea
$$

The cross term vanishes, and this time not by independence
but because the expected prediction is the expectation of the prediction.
The first factor is a constant, so it comes out of the expectation:

$$
\ba
\E{2 \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \Epredval} \paren{\Epredval - \predval}}
&= 2 \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \Epredval} \E{\Epredval - \predval}
&& \text{(constant factors)} \\
&= 2 \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \Epredval} \paren{\E{\Epredval} - \E{\predval}}
&& \text{(linearity)} \\
&= 2 \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \Epredval} \paren{\Epredval - \E{\predval}}
&& \text{(expectation of a constant)} \\
&= 2 \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \Epredval} \paren{\Epredval - \Epredval}
&& \text{(definition of the expected prediction)} \\
&= 2 \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \Epredval} \cdot 0
&& \text{(} a - a = 0 \text{)} \\
&= 0
&& \text{(a number times zero)}
\ea
$$

The third term is the expectation of the squared deviation of the prediction from its mean,
which is the
[variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance)
of the prediction:

$$
\ba
\E{\sqf{\Epredval - \predval}}
&= \E{\sqf{\predval - \Epredval}}
&& \text{(a number and its negative have the same square)} \\
&= \Var{\predval}
&& \text{(definition of variance)}
\ea
$$

Adding the three expectations,

$$
\E{\sqf{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \predval}}
= \sqf{\bias{\predval}} + \Var{\predval}.
$$ {#eq-epe-after-bias}

Neither cross term needed the noise to be normal,
and neither assumed anything about the fitting procedure:
$\fitproc$ can be a line, a tree or a neural network.
This split is specific to squared-error loss, the loss of this chapter's examples.

:::
